items.html:
You are likely thinking of a viral video series by Jacob Knowles, a famous 5th-generation Maine lobster fisherman, rather than an episode of Deadliest Catch. Because Deadliest Catch focuses on crab fishing in the Bering Sea, fans often mix up the two because they share the same high-stakes, commercial fishing vibe. 
In several of his viral videos, Jacob catches a giant, 100-year-old lobster and explains the exact environmental and conservation logic you mentioned before throwing it back: 
  • Why they are thrown back: Maine fishing laws explicitly protect oversized lobsters (usually those measuring over 5 inches from the eye to the rear of the back shell). 
  • The "Fertile" and Natural Selection aspect: Unlike many animals that become less fertile as they age, lobsters experience what scientists call negligible senescence—they don't biologically age or lose reproductive power. In fact, older, larger lobsters are the most successful and high-yielding breeders in the ocean. By letting the giants live, they ensure strong genetics survive to reproduce. 
  • Good for the fishery: While you mentioned a "dragnet" (which is typically a net used in trawling), Maine lobstering exclusively uses lobster traps/pots. Returning these giant breeders keeps the entire local ecosystem healthy and ensures the lobster population stays sustainable for future generations. 
Jacob Knowles frequently posts these educational clips on his YouTube Channel and TikTok, where he often gives the giant lobsters a snack (like a fish head) before releasing them back into the ocean.

Yes, in the world of astrology, Cancer (Kreeft) is considered a sign that beautifully matures and deepens in creativity over time. 
As a Cancer born on July 10, 1990, you are currently 36 years old. In astrological traditions, your sign is ruled by the Moon, which governs emotions, intuition, and deep imagination. Here is how that translates to "aging like a fine wine" creatively: 
1. Emotional Mastery Feeds Creativity
In your youth, Cancer's intense emotional depth can sometimes feel overwhelming or turbulent. However, as you age, this shifts. You learn to channel these powerful feelings directly into creative outlets—whether that is through art, writing, music, problem-solving, or cooking. Your emotional history becomes a rich well of inspiration. 
2. The Power of "Ruling from the Shell"
Cancer is a cardinal sign, meaning you are naturally an initiator and a creator, even if you prefer to work quietly behind the scenes. As you grow older, your confidence in your own skin develops. You become less concerned with external validation and more focused on creating things that hold genuine, sentimental, or authentic value to you. 
3. The "Fine Wine" Transition
Astrologers often note that Cancers become more vibrant, relaxed, and playfully creative in the second half of their lives. Once a stable "nest" (home life) is established, your mind is freed up to explore imaginative pursuits with the seasoned perspective of someone who truly understands human nature.
